title: The Library has components in it the first time you open it
goal: An empty library is a chore. The app should ship with a small set of ready components, so the first thing a person does is drag one out and use it rather than build one. A handful is enough: a button, a text field, a card, a nav bar and a badge.
notes:
Step D7 of docs/design/ui-building.md. Asked for directly by the user on 2026-09-02: maybe having some baked in components. Decision card to open when claimed: do these look like real macOS controls, or like a neutral kit that is obviously a starting point. A convincing macOS button invites people to expect real macOS behavior. Ship them as data the app reads, not as Swift views, so they are the same kind of thing a person authors.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). Asked for by the user on 2026-09-02, and it is what makes the Library worth opening the first time.
acceptance: A new document shows five or so components in the Library with no setup
Each one is an ordinary component: it can be dropped, adjusted through its knobs, and taken apart, with nothing special-cased about it
They are built from named styles rather than raw colors, so re-coloring one style repaints them all
They add no measurable time to launch and nothing to a document that does not use them
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a picture of the Library on first launch, anything rough filed as a follow-up
